name: Skat
summary: Three-player German trick-taking card game where one declarer bids and plays alone against two defenders.
rules_text: Skat uses 32 cards (A K Q J 10 9 8 7). For three players, deal ten cards each and two face-down as the Skat; with four, dealer sits out. After dealing, players bid increasing game values in an auction; highest bidder becomes declarer. Declarer may pick up the Skat and discard two cards, except in hand games. Declarer then announces the contract: suit game where four Jacks plus chosen suit are trumps, grand where only Jacks are trumps, or null where there are no trumps and declarer must lose all tricks. The other two form a team and must not communicate. Ten tricks are played, must follow suit if possible. In suit and grand, card points count: Ace 11, Ten 10, King 4, Queen 3, Jack 2, totalling 120. Declarer needs 61 to win, with bonuses for 90 and for taking all tricks. Game value is calculated from base value times multipliers; if bid exceeds actual valueDeclarer loses automatically. Scores accumulate over agreed number of deals.
rating_reason: Classic 3-player bidding trick-taking, numeric bids and hidden hands
